summary.text: A lipid bilayer is a thin polar membrane made of two layers of lipid molecules, and it forms a continuous barrier around all cells.
It keeps ions, proteins and other molecules where they are needed, because it is impermeable to most water-soluble molecules.
When phospholipids are exposed to water, they self-assemble into a two-layered sheet with their hydrophobic tails pointing toward the center.

facts.label: Phospholipid parts
facts.value: A hydrophilic phosphate head and two fatty acid tails

facts.label: Core thickness
facts.value: The hydrophobic core is typically 3-4 nm thick

facts.label: Cholesterol's role
facts.value: Strengthens the bilayer and lowers its permeability in animal cells

facts.label: Scale
facts.value: On a watermelon-sized cell, it would be paper-thin

facts.label: Hard to study
facts.value: Needs electron microscopy or atomic force microscopy

items.prompt: Phospholipids are mixed into water. Each has a water-loving head and a water-avoiding tail. How do they arrange themselves?

options.label: Into a single sheet, with the tails facing the water
Into a double sheet, heads facing the water and tails tucked together in the middle
Into a double sheet, with the tails facing out toward the water
Into a random cluster with no layers at all

items.explain: Exposed to water, phospholipids form a two-layered sheet with the hydrophobic tails pointing toward the center.

items.prompt: A cell must keep its salt balance and pH steady even though its boundary nearly blocks salt particles. How does it manage?

options.label: It moves ions across the bilayer using proteins called ion pumps
It lets ions diffuse freely through the middle of the bilayer
It dissolves the ions in the hydrophobic tails
It thickens the bilayer whenever salt levels rise

items.explain: Bilayers are particularly impermeable to ions, so cells regulate salt concentrations and pH by transporting ions across with ion pumps.

items.prompt: Which molecule found in animal cell membranes helps strengthen the bilayer and make it less permeable?

options.label: Ion pumps, by sealing gaps between lipids
Water, by filling the center of the bilayer
Cholesterol
A lipid tail, by turning into a head

items.explain: In animal cells, cholesterol helps strengthen the bilayer and decrease its permeability.

items.prompt: A lab-made bilayer is cooled well below normal. What change may it go through?

options.label: The heads and tails swap sides
It dissolves into the surrounding water
It splits into separate single layers
It can shift from a fluid state into a solid gel

items.explain: A bilayer can adopt a solid gel phase at lower temperatures and become fluid at higher temperatures.

items.prompt: Chemists analyse the two faces of the membrane of a human red blood cell. What do they find?

options.label: The inner and outer leaflets have different lipid compositions
Both leaflets contain exactly the same lipids
Only the outer leaflet contains any phospholipids
The inner leaflet is made of protein, not lipid

items.explain: In many natural bilayers, including human red blood cells, the inner and outer leaflets differ in composition.

items.prompt: A sperm joins an egg during fertilization, and a virus gets into a cell. What do both rely on?

options.label: Ion pumps that pull the two cells into one
Cholesterol that melts the bilayers apart
Certain membrane proteins that fuse two bilayers together
Phospholipids that flip heads and tails

items.explain: Certain membrane proteins fuse two bilayers together, as in the acrosome reaction and the entry of a virus into a cell.
